name: Humanoid robot key component stack
description: A commercial humanoid robot platform component stack for early fleet deployment: actuators, hands, battery and power, thermal management, sensing, onboard compute, control software, structure, safety, manufacturing, and service. This is a paid-domain candidate map, not a reviewed investment product.

targetContext.targetScale: pilot fleets to early 10k-unit/year manufacturing programs
targetContext.targetPerformance: human-scale biped mobility, useful manipulation, safe operation around people, multi-hour duty cycle
targetContext.targetUseCase: industrial, logistics, and service tasks in human-designed spaces
targetContext.region: US users researching global suppliers and listed exposure

name: Human-form-factor workforce automation capability
description: The demand-side capability: robots that can use human-centric spaces, tools, and task flows without redesigning every workplace.

name: Actuation system
description: Joint modules, reducers, motors, bearings, encoders, and drive electronics. It bottlenecks payload, walking stability, duty cycle, noise, and service life.

metrics.name: Humanoid actuation subsystem cost magnitude
metrics.description: V0 order-of-magnitude estimate for the full actuation subsystem, anchored to public low-end humanoid robot price and 23-43 joint motor disclosure. Not a confirmed BOM.

name: Dexterous hand and tactile system
description: Hand mechanisms, finger actuation, tactile arrays, slip detection, and local hand control. It determines whether the robot can do useful manipulation rather than only locomotion demos.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Public humanoid sources do not break out hand mechanics, tactile sensors, local control, reliability qualification, and integration as a reviewed component price.

name: Battery, power, and charging system
description: Cell selection, pack architecture, BMS, power distribution, docking, and certification. It gates runtime, fleet uptime, abuse tolerance, and deployability.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed public humanoid sources identify battery/runtime and charging constraints, but do not break out pack, BMS, docking, certification, and fleet-spares cost as a standalone audited subsystem price.

name: Thermal management system
description: Thermal paths for motors, drives, battery, and edge compute. Poor thermal design shortens useful duty cycle and turns demos into short bursts.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed public sources support thermal constraints around motors, batteries, and compute, but not a standalone humanoid thermal BOM, qualification, and service cost.

name: Perception and sensing stack
description: Cameras, depth, LiDAR, IMU, encoders, force/torque, tactile, proximity, and audio sensing. Sensor alignment and drift become control errors at the body level.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Public sources list sensing and perception ingredients, but not the audited cost of sensor fusion, calibration, drift control, and replacement for a commercial humanoid fleet.

name: Onboard compute and control electronics
description: Edge AI compute, real-time controllers, motor-control networking, power isolation, and safety electronics. It must fit autonomy into a tight power and heat envelope.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed public sources support onboard compute and controller roles, but not a separated controller, safety electronics, networking, and power-isolation cost for humanoid production.

name: Structure, materials, and harness
description: Skeleton, enclosures, skin, cable routing, connectors, feet, and serviceable modules. Weight, stiffness, wire fatigue, and assembly tolerance decide real fleet reliability.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed sources support structure, battery, safety, and certification roles, but not an audited structure, harness, connector, enclosure, and serviceability cost as a separate subsystem.

name: Locomotion and whole-body control software
description: Whole-body control, balance, gait, state estimation, contact control, fall recovery, and runtime safety monitoring.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices whole-body control, balance, fall recovery, field validation, and runtime safety monitoring separately from the full humanoid program.

name: Manipulation AI and data stack
description: Vision-language-action policies, grasp planning, teleoperation data, imitation/RL training, task planning, and fleet learning.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source breaks out manipulation policy, teleoperation data, simulation, fleet learning, and validation cost from the complete humanoid robot program.

name: Manufacturing, test, safety, and service
description: Assembly, calibration, burn-in, traceability, functional safety, E-stop, duty-cycle validation, field service, and spares loops.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices the combined assembly, calibration, burn-in, traceability, functional-safety, field-service, and spares loop per humanoid robot.

name: Rotary joint module
description: Torque-dense rotary joint for shoulders, hips, wrists, and ankles. It gates useful payload because motor, reducer, bearing, encoder, drive, heat path, and harness must fit inside one serviceable joint.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Public humanoid sources do not break out rotary joint BOM, yield, burn-in, service spares, and actuator-level qualification as an audited module price.

name: Linear joint module
description: High-force linear actuator path for legs, knees, torso, or high-load axes. It is hard to clear because screw life, shock loads, lubrication, sealing, and compact packaging all affect field reliability.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices humanoid linear actuator assemblies, fatigue validation, sealing, lubrication, and field-replacement cost separately.

name: Reducer and transmission stack
description: Strain-wave, planetary, cycloidal, or screw transmission choices that set backlash, stiffness, torque density, and lifetime. The bottleneck is not only precision; it is repeatable joint-grade quality, lifecycle validation, and enough qualified suppliers for humanoid-scale actuator volumes.

metrics.name: Humanoid reducer and transmission stack cost magnitude
metrics.description: V0 order-of-magnitude estimate for multiple precision reducer/transmission elements across a humanoid actuation stack. Not a confirmed BOM or supplier quote.

name: Motor stack
description: Frameless BLDC, direct-drive, or quasi-direct-drive motors sized for compact torque and heat rejection. Motor choice gates noise, duty cycle, efficiency, magnet exposure, and actuator thermal headroom.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Public sources support humanoid motor and joint counts, but do not disclose audited motor-stack BOM, magnet sourcing, winding yield, thermal margin, or service-spares cost.

name: Motor drive power electronics
description: Gate drivers, current sensing, inverter power stage, protection, EMI filtering, and control loops for many distributed joints.

name: Joint sensing and feedback
description: Absolute encoders, torque sensing, current sensing, temperature sensing, and calibration model for closed-loop force and position control.

name: Joint bearings and sealing
description: Thin-section bearings, cross-roller bearings, seals, lubrication, and shock handling inside compact joints. It gates fleet reliability because impact, dust, wire motion, and maintenance access turn commodity bearings into joint-specific qualification work.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source breaks out humanoid joint bearing, sealing, lubrication, shock qualification, and replacement-rate cost as a standalone subsystem.

name: Strain-wave reducer
description: Compact high-ratio reducer option with low backlash but lifetime and cost pressure at humanoid volumes.

name: Planetary roller screw
description: High-force linear conversion component whose precision thread grinding and fatigue life can become high-load actuator bottlenecks.

name: Frameless BLDC torque motor
description: Compact permanent-magnet motor integrated into joint housings.

name: Rare-earth magnet supply
description: NdFeB-class magnet supply that affects compact motors and geopolitical supply risk.

name: Joint inverter power stage
description: MOSFET/GaN power stage sized for compact multi-axis joint current control.

name: Current sensing and gate driver
description: High-bandwidth current sensing and gate drive electronics required for stable torque control and protection.

name: EMI filtering and grounding
description: Distributed motor-drive EMI control across dense wiring and sensors.

name: Five-finger hand mechanism
description: Multi-DoF hand mechanism for object handling, tool use, and human-like workspace compatibility. It gates usefulness because finger packaging, actuation, tactile routing, breakage, and replacement cost decide whether manipulation survives outside demos.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Public humanoid sources do not disclose an audited five-finger hand BOM, actuator count, tactile integration, field breakage, or spare-hand cost.

name: Tendon or cable hand transmission
description: Remote-drive hand transmission that saves finger volume but adds routing, stretch, friction, and calibration issues.

name: Micro hand actuator
description: Small motor, gearbox, leadscrew, or tendon drive packaged in the hand and wrist volume.

name: Fingertip tactile array
description: Dense pressure/shear sensing at the fingertip for slip detection and grasp control.

name: Palm force and tactile array
description: Palm contact sensing for stable large-object manipulation and safe human interaction.

name: Slip detection policy
description: Control method converting tactile streams into grip adjustments before objects fall.

name: Lithium-ion cell selection
description: Cell chemistry and format trade-off across energy density, discharge power, safety, and cycle life.

name: Battery pack enclosure and interconnect
description: Mechanical pack, interconnect, fuse, contactor, sealing, and abuse protection for a moving robot body. It gates runtime and safety because pack packaging must absorb falls, thermal events, high-current transients, and fast service swaps.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed sources support battery/runtime constraints, but not an audited humanoid pack enclosure, interconnect, protection, certification, and replacement cost.

name: Battery management system
description: Cell monitoring, balancing, state estimation, protection, diagnostics, and certification interface.

name: High-current power distribution bus
description: Distributed high-current power routing, conversion, protection, and isolation between pack, compute, and joints.

name: Charging and docking interface
description: Fleet charging dock, contact alignment, battery swap or charging control, and service ergonomics. It gates uptime because robots that cannot self-dock, charge safely, and return to service create hidden operator labor.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices humanoid charging docks, automatic alignment, connector life, battery-swap workflow, or fleet charger deployment cost.

name: Battery pack safety certification
description: UN38.3, UL-class, transport, abuse, and functional safety requirements for mobile robot batteries.

name: Motor and joint thermal path
description: Heat conduction from winding, drive, gearbox, and bearing stack to housing without creating touch-temperature or reliability issues.

name: Battery thermal safety
description: Cell temperature monitoring, heat spreading, runaway containment, and pack-level shutoff.

name: Compute heat spreader
description: Thermal interface, heat spreader, and sink path for edge AI modules inside torso/head volume.

name: Airflow or liquid cooling loop
description: Fan, duct, heat-pipe, cold plate, or liquid loop design constrained by noise, dust, impact, and service. It gates sustained work because motors, drives, battery, and edge compute create heat in a sealed moving body.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: Reviewed sources support humanoid thermal constraints, but not an audited airflow, heat-pipe, cold-plate, liquid-loop, acoustic, and service cost.

name: Thermal sensor map
description: Thermistors and IC temperature sensors across pack, motors, drivers, compute, and enclosure hot spots.

name: Sustained duty-cycle validation
description: Thermal and reliability test process proving a robot can work useful shifts, not only short demos.

name: Stereo RGB camera module
description: Head or torso cameras for perception, teleoperation, and scene understanding.

name: Depth camera and 3D LiDAR
description: Depth sensing for navigation, obstacle avoidance, and manipulation workspace estimation.

name: IMU attitude sensing
description: Inertial sensing for balance, state estimation, impact detection, and fall recovery.

name: Joint encoder and position sensing
description: Absolute or incremental joint feedback needed for stable body control and calibration.

name: Force and torque sensing
description: Foot, wrist, and joint force sensing for contact-aware locomotion and manipulation.

name: Proximity and touch safety sensing
description: Close-range detection and contact sensing for human-robot interaction and collision mitigation.

name: Audio and microphone array
description: Speech, command, and situational awareness sensing for human-centric deployment.

name: Edge AI compute module
description: On-robot AI accelerator or SoC that runs perception, policy inference, and local planning within power and heat limits.

name: Real-time MCU and safety controller
description: Deterministic controller path for motor loops, E-stop, safe torque off, and health monitoring.

name: Motor-control network
description: Deterministic communication from central controller to many distributed motor drivers and sensor boards.

name: Time sync and sensor fusion
description: Timestamping, synchronization, calibration, and fusion of camera, IMU, encoder, force, and tactile streams.

name: Safety power isolation
description: Power isolation and protection architecture separating battery, high-current joints, compute, and safety logic.

name: Lightweight skeleton frame
description: Aluminum, magnesium, steel, polymer, or composite structure balancing weight, stiffness, impact, and manufacturability.

name: Torso enclosure and protective skin
description: Protective external surfaces that package compute, power, sensors, fans, and safe human contact.

name: Wiring harness and connectors
description: High-flex harness, connectors, strain relief, and service routing through moving limbs. It gates reliability because every joint adds bend cycles, EMI, connector retention, and service-routing failure modes.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices high-flex humanoid harnessing, connector qualification, strain relief, EMI control, and service routing as a separate subsystem.

name: High-stiffness low-mass materials
description: Material set for limbs and torso where weight, stiffness, fatigue, cost, and manufacturability collide.

name: Foot contact structure
description: Foot sole, compliance, force sensing, tread, and replacement design for walking and balance.

name: Serviceable modular design
description: Architecture that lets fleet operators replace joints, hands, packs, sensors, and limbs without rebuilding the robot.

name: Whole-body control stack
description: Coordinated control of limbs, torso, hands, contacts, and center of mass.

name: Gait and balance policy
description: Walking, standing, stepping, push recovery, and uneven-floor policies.

name: Simulation-to-real training pipeline
description: Physics simulation, domain randomization, policy transfer, and hardware validation loop.

name: Contact force control
description: Force-position control for safe grasping, pushing, leaning, and foot-ground interaction.

name: Fall recovery and safe stop
description: Detection, controlled stopping, recovery, and service handoff for falls or unstable states.

name: Runtime safety monitor
description: Independent health and safety monitor for torque, temperature, battery, perception, and human proximity constraints.

name: Vision-language-action policy model
description: Embodied AI model that maps instructions and perception to action sequences.

name: Grasp planning policy
description: Planning and control for hand approach, grasp choice, grip adjustment, and release.

name: Teleoperation data collection
description: Human demonstration capture used to train manipulation and task policies.

name: Imitation and reinforcement-learning loop
description: Training loop for converting demonstrations, rewards, simulation, and fleet failures into policies.

name: Task planning and execution
description: Breaking user goals into perception, motion, grasp, tool, and verification steps.

name: Manipulation benchmark and evaluation
description: Task suite, metrics, data replay, and failure taxonomy for judging useful manipulation.

name: High-volume joint assembly
description: Assembly of motors, reducers, bearings, sensors, drives, harness, and housings at repeatable quality.

name: End-of-line calibration rig
description: Factory system for joint zeroing, torque calibration, sensor alignment, battery checks, and whole-body validation.

name: Battery pack end-of-line test
description: Pack electrical, thermal, balancing, safety, leakage, and charge/discharge validation before robot integration.

name: Whole-robot burn-in
description: Factory burn-in process for thermal soak, motion cycles, sensor drift, and early-life failures.

name: Reliability and MTBF tracking
description: Fleet telemetry and root-cause loop for joint, hand, battery, thermal, and sensor failures.

name: Functional safety and E-stop
description: Safety architecture for stop states, safe torque off, power isolation, human proximity, and incident logging.

name: Field service and spares loop
description: Service workflow for replacement joints, hands, batteries, sensors, calibration, and refurbishment. It gates TCO because a pilot fleet becomes expensive if failures require factory return or manual recalibration.

metrics.name: Cost disclosure
metrics.description: No reviewed public source prices humanoid field-service labor, spares pool, calibration workflow, refurbishment, and replacement-cycle cost.

name: Flexspline (thin-wall flexible gear cup)
description: Deformable thin-wall cylindrical steel cup with external teeth that flexes under the wave generator; the highest-fatigue, hardest-to-make member of a strain-wave reducer. Made from precision-forged and heat-treated maraging or alloy steel, then gear-cut and ground. Industry basis: the strain-wave (strain-wave gearing) standard defines the reducer as exactly three parts - wave generator, flexspline, and circular spline - and flexspline fatigue life is the gear's life-limiter, the manufacturing bottleneck targeted by multiple flexspline-fabrication patents (e.g. metal AM, bulk-metallic-glass routes).
notes: Hard to develop: the flexspline endures billions of flex cycles, so its fatigue strength sets the whole reducer's service life. Precision forging/heat-treat plus matched gear grinding of a thin-wall cup is the gating manufacturing step and the subject of active patent activity. Likely citable source: strain-wave-gear vendor technical pages; USPTO US11839927 'Methods for fabricating strain wave gear flexsplines'. Qualitative only this pass (no quantified fatigue-life claim).

name: Circular spline (rigid internal ring gear)
description: Rigid outer ring with internal teeth (two more teeth than the flexspline) that meshes with the deformed flexspline; a precision gear-hobbed and ground hardened-steel ring. Industry basis: second of the three canonical strain-wave reducer members; the tooth-count differential of two versus the flexspline sets the reduction ratio and requires matched precision gear grinding with the flexspline.

name: Wave generator (elliptical cam + flex bearing)
description: Elliptical steel cam fitted with a thin, elliptically deformable ball bearing that imposes the travelling deflection wave on the flexspline; combines a centric cam plug and a specialty deformable bearing. Industry basis: third canonical strain-wave reducer member, commonly described as a centric hub plus a special thin, elliptically deformable ball bearing; the flex (deformable) bearing is itself a specialty item that few makers produce.
notes: Hard to develop: the elliptically deformable thin-section ball bearing on the wave generator is a specialty bearing few suppliers can make, and it is a wear/life driver for the reducer. Likely citable source: strain-wave-gear vendor technology pages; Sumitomo Drive strain-wave gearboxes. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Output cross-roller bearing (thin-section)
description: Single-row crossed-roller bearing that carries the joint's combined moment, radial, and axial load in a slim envelope, integrated into the strain-wave reducer output or the joint housing. RA-series thin-section sizes are the documented humanoid hip/shoulder parts. Industry basis: industrial robot joints primarily use cross-roller bearings for high stiffness under multi-axis loads; the qualified maker set is concentrated (THK, IKO, Schaeffler/INA, plus the reducer's integrated bearing), which under ADR-0005 makes it a concentration-override decomposition-eligible component.
notes: Hard to develop: a thin-section crossed-roller bearing must hold high moment stiffness and low cross-axis play in a slim ring; qualification is concentrated among a few specialty bearing makers. Likely citable source: 2026 robotic-joint bearing guides citing RA5008/RA10008 for humanoid shoulder/hip joints; THK/IKO crossed-roller catalogs. Verify the specific RA-size humanoid claim and maker concentration in the later evidence pass. Qualitative only this pass. Exposure overflow (>5 makers, soft cap): Harmonic Drive Systems also integrates an output cross-roller bearing inside its strain-wave reducers, but as the captive/integrated option it is the breadth tail behind the merchant pair THK + IKO and the second-source set Schaeffler/NSK/NTN; not wired as a separate supplier edge to keep the node at the 5 most-concentrated makers.

name: High-cleanliness bearing steel (100Cr6 / GCr15)
description: Through-hardening chromium bearing steel (DIN 100Cr6 / GB GCr15 / AISI 52100) with controlled oxygen and inclusion cleanliness; feedstock for cross-roller bearings, the wave-generator flex bearing, and roller-screw rollers. Industry basis: 100Cr6/GCr15/52100 is the standard precision-bearing steel and bearing fatigue life scales with steel cleanliness (vacuum-degassed / VIM-VAR grades), so premium-clean bearing steel is supplied by a short list of specialty mills, making it a supply-concentrated feedstock chokepoint.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck' so it renders as a real feedstock node: premium-clean bearing steel cleanliness gates bearing/roller fatigue life and is a short-list specialty-mill supply. Parented under the reducer (depth 4) and reused by the roller-screw rollers; deliberately NOT parented under the flexspline (that would push it past the depth-4 render budget). Likely citable source: ISO 683-17 bearing steels; specialty-steel cleanliness datasheets (e.g. Ovako / Proterial). Qualitative only this pass.

name: Roller-screw threaded shaft (central screw)
description: Central screw with a precision multi-start thread that the planetary rollers ride; the precision-ground core of a planetary roller screw. Industry basis: patent and vendor decomposition describe a planetary roller screw as 'a screw with an outer thread, a nut, and a plurality of longitudinal rollers'; dedicated thread-grinding machines (e.g. EMAG WPG) are marketed specifically for roller-screw shafts with the highest precision requirements for humanoid-robot linear actuators.
notes: Hard to develop: the multi-start shaft thread must be ground to sub-micron-class tolerance and matched to the rollers and nut; thread-grinding capacity is the upstream gate (existing thread_grinding_equipment node). Likely citable source: EMAG planetary-roller-screw grinding (WPG 7); USPTO US11994191 'Planetary roller screw'. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Planetary rollers (single-start grooved rollers)
description: Set of threaded rollers between screw and nut with a convex single-start profile that multiplies contact points for high force density; precision-ground and profile-matched to the nut thread. Industry basis: roller threads must have a consistent convex profile with an angle matching the nut thread to distribute contact stress; roller grinding is the hardest step and gates output volume for roller-screw makers.
notes: Hard to develop: grinding a consistent convex single-start roller profile at volume is the throughput-limiting step in roller-screw production. Rollers are 52100-class bearing steel (reuses the bearing-steel feedstock). Likely citable source: linearmotiontips.com roller-screw performance; USPTO US11994191. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Roller-screw nut (internal-thread + ring gears)
description: Coaxial nut with an internal multi-start thread and integrated ring gears that time the rollers; precision-machined hardened steel, often with an internal gear ring and a retainer/cage. Industry basis: roller-screw assemblies are described as 'a nut mounted coaxially around the screw with an inner thread' plus 'an internal gear ring and a retainer or cage'; integrated-ring-gear roller-screw manufacture is covered by patent (e.g. US10041573).

name: Coreless / hollow-cup micro motor
description: Small coreless (ironless-rotor) brushed or slotless BLDC motor that drives one hand degree of freedom, chosen for low inertia and high acceleration in a forearm-mounted actuator pack. Industry basis: the 2025-2026 Tesla Optimus Gen-3 hand uses a hollow-cup-motor + lead-screw + rope-drive scheme with roughly a dozen-plus coreless/slotless motors per hand and actuators relocated to the forearm; maxon and Shenzhen PICEA Motion are named coreless-motor suppliers.
notes: Architecture-level claim grounded in 2025-2026 Optimus Gen-3 hand-redesign coverage; exact per-hand motor counts kept qualitative (cited as a range, not asserted as fact). Likely citable source: robottoday.com Optimus hand redesign (hollow cup + lead screw + rope); foxtechrobotics.com dexterous-hand insight. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Hand micro lead-screw / ball-screw drive
description: Miniature lead or ball screw that converts the hollow-cup motor's rotation into the linear pull on a finger tendon; the rotary-to-linear stage of each finger drive. Industry basis: Optimus Gen-3 hand reporting describes motor rotation converted into linear motion through a screw that then pulls the tendon connected to the finger bones, with the hand likely adopting a gearbox + lead-screw + tendon drive.
notes: Hard to develop: packaging a precision miniature lead/ball screw at fingertip scale with adequate life is an active design frontier; reuses precision-screw know-how. Likely citable source: robottoday.com Optimus hand redesign; optimusk.blog Optimus hardware specs. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Fingertip tactile sensing element (MEMS / magnetic / visuotactile)
description: The transducer inside the fingertip tactile array - a MEMS barometric/capacitive die, a magnetic (Hall) tactile cell, or a camera-based visuotactile module - that converts contact force and slip into signals. Industry basis: tactile fingertip sensors provide the force-feedback hardware in each fingertip and tactile sensing is a named critical enabler for dexterous manipulation; suppliers in graph include PaXini, XELA Robotics (tactile), and TE Connectivity (force).
notes: Hard to develop: durable, high-density, low-drift fingertip tactile transduction (whether MEMS, magnetic, or visuotactile) is one of the least-mature dexterous-manipulation enablers. Likely citable source: foxtechrobotics.com dexterous-hand sensing; arXiv Bowden-cable hand work. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Cathode active material (high-nickel NMC)
description: Nickel-rich layered-oxide (NMC, e.g. ~8:1:1 Ni:Mn:Co) cathode powder that sets the cell's energy density and the bulk of its cost and pulls in nickel/cobalt/lithium feedstock. Industry basis: a Li-ion cell comprises cathode + anode + separator + electrolyte, and high-energy humanoid cells run NMC chemistries; the cathode is the dominant cost and energy driver of the cell, and its precursor/active-material supply is concentrated.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': cathode active material dominates cell cost/energy and its high-nickel precursor supply is concentrated. Likely citable source: humanoid battery-pack design notes; cathode-materials reviews. Qualitative only this pass (no quantified Wh/kg or composition asserted as fact).

name: Anode active material (graphite / Si-blend)
description: Graphite (natural or synthetic) anode material, increasingly with a silicon additive for capacity; the second core electrode material of the cell. Industry basis: the anode is one of the four canonical cell components, and silicon-blended graphite is the route to the higher gravimetric energy that humanoid duty cycles demand; graphite supply (especially synthetic and high-purity natural) is geographically concentrated.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': graphite (and Si-blend) anode supply is concentrated and gates energy density. Likely citable source: humanoid battery-pack design notes; humanoid battery program writeups. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Battery separator (microporous polyolefin)
description: Microporous PE/PP film, often ceramic-coated, that prevents anode-cathode contact while passing ions; a safety-critical, supply-concentrated specialty film. Industry basis: the separator prevents the cathode from directly contacting the anode while allowing current-carrying ions to pass, and high-power separator film is a recognized chokepoint with few qualified makers.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': qualified high-power separator film is a recognized few-supplier chokepoint and a safety-critical component. Likely citable source: humanoid battery-pack design notes; humanoid battery design-challenge writeups. Qualitative only this pass.

name: BMS analog front-end / fuel-gauge IC
description: Multi-cell monitoring analog front-end (AFE) IC that measures per-cell voltage, temperature, and current and balances cells; the silicon heart of the battery-management module. Industry basis: the BMS monitors cell voltages, temperature, and current and balances load, and AFE/fuel-gauge ICs are supplied by a short list of vendors (TI, Analog Devices, NXP); Texas Instruments and NXP are already in the graph.

name: Electrical (silicon) steel laminations
description: Thin grain-oriented or non-oriented Si-Fe laminations stacked to form the motor stator/rotor core; low-loss electrical steel is a supply-concentrated specialty. Industry basis: frameless torque motors use laminated electrical-steel cores, and thin high-grade non-oriented electrical steel for high-speed robot motors is made by a short list of mills (Nippon Steel, POSCO, JFE, Baowu); raw-material lists for robot motors include iron/steel and copper.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': thin high-grade non-oriented electrical steel for high-speed robot motors is a short-list specialty-mill supply and a real upstream constraint. Renders at depth 4 under the frameless BLDC motor. Likely citable source: non-oriented electrical-steel grade datasheets (Nippon Steel / POSCO). Qualitative only this pass.

name: Copper magnet (enamelled) wire
description: Insulated copper winding wire for the motor stator coils; gauge and insulation class set slot fill and thermal rating. Industry basis: copper magnet wire is the universal motor-winding material and an explicit raw-material input to robot/EV motors; slot fill and insulation class gate torque density and duty cycle. Per ADR-0005 this is kept as a material leaf (commodity at ingot/wire level) rather than over-decomposed, absent a specific robot-grade specialty corner.
notes: Deliberately NOT key-tagged: copper magnet wire is largely commodity, so per ADR-0005 it stays a material leaf and does not render on the canvas. It is recorded for completeness and exposure, not to lift the rendered count. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Sintered NdFeB magnet feedstock (Nd2Fe14B + Dy/Tb)
description: Sintered neodymium-iron-boron magnet blanks (with Dy/Tb for high-temperature coercivity) - the upstream feedstock that the rare-earth magnet supply node converts into finished arc magnets. Industry basis: NdFeB (Nd2Fe14B) is the highest-energy-product permanent magnet and the standard robot-motor magnet, with Dy/Tb heavy-rare-earth additions raising coercivity for hot joint motors; sintered-magnet feedstock supply is a recognized China-concentrated chokepoint.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': sintered NdFeB feedstock (and its heavy-rare-earth Dy/Tb content) is a China-concentrated supply chokepoint. Deepens the existing rare-earth magnet supply node by one upstream layer; renders at depth 4. Likely citable source: NdFeB magnet references (MP Materials, Arnold Magnetics). Qualitative only this pass.

name: Sensor elastic element (compliant spoke / Maltese-cross body)
description: Precision-machined metal elastic body (spoke / Maltese-cross / compliant-beam form) whose strain encodes the six-axis load; the mechanical core of a force/torque sensor. Industry basis: six-axis force/torque sensors use precision-machined elastic bodies with metallic strain gauges arranged on them to form multiple Wheatstone bridges, and the elastic-element design (low cross-axis coupling) is the core IP of the sensor.
notes: Hard to develop: designing an elastic element with high sensitivity and low cross-axis coupling, then machining it precisely, is the core force/torque sensor IP. Likely citable source: optimized six-axis F/T sensor papers; ScienceDirect compliant six-axis sensor work. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Strain transducer (foil gauge / silicon piezoresistor)
description: Foil strain gauges or silicon piezoresistive die bonded to the elastic element and wired into Wheatstone bridges; the transduction element of the force/torque sensor. Industry basis: strain gauges are attached to the beam surfaces of the elastic element to form Wheatstone bridges, and MEMS variants use ion-implanted piezoresistors; bridge trimming and gauge bonding are the precision manufacturing steps.

name: Magnetic encoder ASIC (Hall array) + diametric magnet
description: A diametrically polarized magnet rotating above an ASIC Hall-sensor array that resolves absolute angle; the dominant compact robot-joint encoder type. Industry basis: a small diametrically polarized magnet rotates above an ASIC containing an array of Hall-effect sensors and generates a voltage as it rotates, and magnetic encoder ASICs are supplied by a short list of vendors (e.g. AMS-OSRAM, Renishaw, MPS).

name: Optical code disk + photodetector (high-res absolute, output-side option)
description: Etched glass or metal code disk read by an LED/photodetector array for high-resolution absolute position where magnetic resolution is insufficient, used as the output-side encoder in dual-encoder designs (not a universal requirement on every joint). Industry basis: optical encoders include a disc/code-plate, a sensor, and a processor, with absolute optical encoders using concentric patterns where each tic gives a unique binary code; output-side optical encoders co-exist with motor-side magnetic ones in documented hybrid designs.
notes: Framed as the high-resolution / output-side option (dual-encoder designs), NOT asserted as present on every humanoid joint, to stay honest about coverage. Likely citable source: robot-sensor surveys; USPTO US11002562 hybrid magnetic+optical encoder. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Magnesium alloy (die-cast structural)
description: Lightest structural metal (density ~1.8 g/cm3) used for skeletal/joint housings and shells to cut mass and aid thermal spreading. Industry basis: magnesium alloys are described as a core material in Tesla Optimus Gen 2, helping reduce component weight and enhance thermal management. Per ADR-0005 kept as a material leaf (commodity at ingot level) absent a robot-specific cast-Mg specialty corner.
notes: Deliberately NOT key-tagged: structural Mg alloy is commodity at ingot level, so per ADR-0005 it stays a material leaf and does not render. Recorded for grounding and exposure (Optimus-specific coverage). Qualitative only this pass (density stated qualitatively).

name: PEEK / carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer
description: High-performance thermoplastic (PEEK), often carbon-fiber-reinforced, for joint mechanisms, brackets, and wear parts - metal-like specific strength at low mass. Industry basis: PEEK offers specific strength exceeding many conventional metals and is used in skeletal structures and joint mechanisms, often reinforced with carbon fiber; Victrex (PEEK) and Evonik are already suppliers in the graph, and qualified high-performance PEEK supply is concentrated.
notes: Key-tagged 'bottleneck': aerospace/robotics-grade PEEK and CF-reinforced PEEK supply is concentrated (e.g. Victrex, Evonik) and is a genuine specialty-materials corner. Renders at depth 3 under the torso enclosure. Likely citable source: PEEK-for-humanoid-robot materials writeups. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Aerospace/structural aluminum alloy
description: Machined or cast aluminum alloy (density ~2.7 g/cm3, roughly one-third that of steel) for primary frame members and brackets. Industry basis: aluminum alloys have about one-third the density of steel and offer good casting, machinability, and corrosion resistance, making them a standard humanoid frame material. Per ADR-0005 kept as a material leaf (commodity at ingot level).
notes: Deliberately NOT key-tagged: structural Al alloy is commodity at ingot level, so per ADR-0005 it stays a material leaf and does not render. Recorded for grounding/exposure. Qualitative only this pass (density stated qualitatively).

name: Power switching device (Si MOSFET / GaN FET)
description: The low-voltage power MOSFET or GaN FET that switches joint-motor phase current and sets inverter efficiency, size, and thermal load. Industry basis: joint inverters for roughly 48 V humanoid motors use low-voltage Si MOSFETs or GaN FETs, with GaN an active power-density frontier; suppliers Infineon, EPC (GaN), Texas Instruments, and STMicroelectronics are all in the graph. Modeled as one device node (Si/GaN) rather than split, to avoid padding.

name: CMOS image sensor + depth emitter (VCSEL / IR)
description: The CMOS/RGBIR image sensor plus the structured-light or time-of-flight emitter (VCSEL/IR) that together form the depth camera's front end. Industry basis: depth-camera reference designs integrate RGBIR image sensors for stereoscopic depth and a ToF LiDAR module, and ToF couples a strobe emitter to a CMOS sensor; depth-sensor suppliers Orbbec, RealSense, and STMicroelectronics are in the graph.

name: MEMS IMU die (gyro + accelerometer)
description: The six-axis MEMS inertial die (three-axis gyroscope plus three-axis accelerometer) inside the IMU module that provides attitude and balance sensing. Industry basis: humanoid sensor sets combine IMU components with depth/stereo sensing, and MEMS IMU dies are supplied by a short list (Bosch Sensortec, STMicro, TDK/InvenSense, ADI); Bosch Sensortec, TDK, and STMicroelectronics are in the graph.

name: Edge AI inference SoC (robot brain)
description: The system-on-chip running onboard perception and vision-language-action inference (e.g. NVIDIA Jetson Thor-class, Qualcomm, Rockchip, D-Robotics); it sets onboard AI throughput within the robot's power budget. Industry basis: humanoid onboard compute is a named SoC chokepoint and the acceptance standard explicitly scopes in the named compute SoC; suppliers NVIDIA (Jetson/Thor), Qualcomm, Rockchip, and D-Robotics are all in the graph.
notes: In-scope per the acceptance standard (the named compute SoC). The full upstream logic-die/HBM fabrication chain lives in the ai_compute_chain domain - this node is the humanoid-side boundary, not a duplicate of that chain. Likely citable source: NVIDIA Jetson Thor / Qualcomm robotics SoC pages. Qualitative only this pass.

name: LPDDR / on-module memory
description: Low-power DRAM (LPDDR5/5X) and storage co-packaged with or beside the inference SoC; it gates on-robot model size and memory bandwidth. Industry basis: edge AI compute modules pair the SoC with LPDDR memory, and memory bandwidth gates on-device model size. This node is kept deliberately shallow: the DRAM/HBM fabrication chain is a documented boundary that lives in the ai_compute_chain domain, so memory is not decomposed further here.
notes: Boundary note (per Day-0 rule, documented boundaries grade as decisions): on-module LPDDR is included as the robot-side memory dependency, but the upstream DRAM/HBM chain is owned by the ai_compute_chain domain - intentionally not decomposed here to avoid scope bleed. Likely citable source: NVIDIA Jetson module LPDDR5 datasheets. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Heat pipe / vapor chamber
description: Sealed two-phase heat-spreader that moves heat from motors or compute to the enclosure or a cooling loop; the workhorse passive thermal path in compact high-duty-cycle robots (not universal on every humanoid). Industry basis: compact high-power electronics use heat pipes and vapor chambers for heat spreading, analogous to the two-phase cooling loop modeled in the flagship; two-phase spreaders are a recognized supply-concentrated item (Aavid/Boyd, Auras, AVC).
notes: Framed as the high-duty-cycle option, not asserted as present on every humanoid, to stay honest about coverage. Likely citable source: heat-pipe/vapor-chamber vendor literature (Boyd/Aavid); high-conductivity thermal-management patents. Qualitative only this pass.

name: Thermal interface material (TIM)
description: Gap-filler, grease, or pad between heat-generating dies/motors and spreaders that sets the contact thermal resistance. Industry basis: TIM is the standard interface between a heat source and a spreader in robot compute and motor thermal paths, and high-performance TIM is a specialty-materials supply (Henkel, Dow, Shin-Etsu); Shin-Etsu is already in the graph.
notes: Deliberately NOT key-tagged this pass: TIM is recorded so existing specialty suppliers (e.g. Shin-Etsu, Henkel) can attach in the exposure pass, but it is counted as a non-rendering material leaf (delta 0) per the plan. Qualitative only this pass.

name: GSA AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG
description: Swiss planetary/satellite roller-screw specialist (Gewinde Satelliten Antriebe AG / Gewinde Ziegler AG, est. 1982). Makes the RGTI inverted planetary roller screw widely reported as the type Tesla sources for Optimus linear actuators; modeled as a near-single-source roller-screw supplier candidate for the humanoid linear-joint stack. Privately held.

name: Rollvis SA
description: Swiss (Geneva, est. 1970) satellite/planetary roller-screw specialist trading as 'Rollvis Swiss'; self-described world leader in satellite roller screws. Together with GSA, frequently cited as holding the majority of the high-precision planetary roller-screw world market — the Swiss near-single-source corner feeding humanoid linear actuators. Privately held.

name: Thread-grinding / ultra-precision CNC grinding equipment
description: Ultra-precision CNC thread-grinding machines that cut the sub-3-micron-tolerance internal and external threads of planetary roller screws (and ball screws). This is the upstream capital-equipment bottleneck behind the Swiss roller-screw corner: the specialized internal-thread grinding expertise and the thin population of qualified grinder builders gate how fast roller-screw capacity can be added for humanoid linear actuators.

name: Drake Manufacturing Services
description: US (Warren, Ohio) builder of precision CNC thread- and gear-grinding machines, including internal thread grinders and ball-nut/ballscrew grinders for the ball-screw and linear-motion industries — the upstream grinding-equipment tier behind roller/ball-screw production. Privately held.

name: PTG Holroyd
description: UK builder of high-precision gear, rotor, screw and thread milling and grinding machines, marketed as producing the world's most accurate helical components — part of the thin population of ultra-precision thread/screw grinder builders upstream of roller-screw production. Part of the Precision Technologies Group; privately held.

name: Shenzhen PICEA Motion (formerly Han's Motion)
description: Shenzhen-based precision harmonic-drive / strain-wave reducer maker, formerly Shenzhen Han's Motion Technology Co., Ltd., rebranded to PICEA Motion. Cited among the global key manufacturers of humanoid-robot harmonic reducers and a Chinese domestic-substitution alternative to Harmonic Drive/Nabtesco. Privately held (some trade sources describe it as a former Han's Laser subsidiary; the company's own site presents it independently).

name: JL MAG Rare-Earth
description: Dual-listed (Shenzhen 300748.SZ / Hong Kong 06680.HK) Chinese sintered-NdFeB permanent-magnet maker; in 2025 upgraded its humanoid-robot magnetic-component R&D department to a dedicated business unit. Magnet output sits inside China's rare-earth export-licensing regime. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
description: Public Tokyo-listed (4063.T) maker of NdFeB (Nd-Fe-B) sintered rare-earth magnets (N Series) used in industrial servomotors and linear motors; operates Japan's large-scale rare-earth separation/refining and is building a heavy-rare-earth refinery to diversify supply off China. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

name: Proterial
description: Private Japanese magnet/materials maker (ex-Hitachi Metals; renamed 2023 after a Bain Capital-led buyout) that pioneered and mass-produces NEOMAX Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets for motors, and mass-produces a heavy-rare-earth-saving grade that minimizes dysprosium/terbium. PRIVATE — no public ticker. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

name: Regal Rexnord
description: Public NYSE-listed (RRX) motion-control group whose brands include Kollmorgen (and Portescap, acquired via the 2023 Altra deal). Kollmorgen frameless / direct-drive torque motors (TBM/KBM/TBM2G) target robot, cobot and humanoid joints. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

name: maxon
description: Private Swiss precision-drive maker; its EC frameless DT torque motors and integrated High Efficiency Joint (HEJ) actuators explicitly target humanoids, quadrupeds and exoskeletons. (Also a hollow-cup/coreless micromotor specialist for dexterous hands.) PRIVATE — no public ticker. Component-exposure candidate; not a confirmed humanoid BOM placement.

name: Netzer Precision
description: Private Israeli maker of contactless capacitive (Electric Encoder) absolute hollow-shaft encoders; immune to magnetic interference near frameless-motor magnets, used in humanoid/space robot arm joints (e.g. NASA Robonaut 2). Supplier candidate.

name: Novanta (ATI Industrial Automation)
description: US NASDAQ-listed precision-technology group; its ATI Industrial Automation division is a long-incumbent maker of multi-axis (six-axis) force/torque sensors for robotic force control, a supplier candidate for humanoid wrist/hand force-torque sensing.

name: Bota Systems
description: Private Swiss (Zurich) maker of compact 6-axis force/torque sensors, torque sensors and tactile sensors for humanoid, medical and collaborative robots (MiniONE, PixONE). Supplier candidate for humanoid force-torque / fingertip sensing.

name: Sunrise Instruments (SRI)
description: Privately-held six-axis force/torque sensor and multi-axis load-cell maker (HQ Canton, Michigan, US; manufacturing in China) with a dedicated humanoid-robot 6-axis force/torque sensor line (C025XX-C060XX). Supplier candidate.

name: XELA Robotics
description: Private (Waseda University spin-out, Tokyo) maker of uSkin high-density three-axis tactile skin sensors covering fingertips, phalanges and palm for humanoid and industrial robot hands/grippers. Supplier candidate for humanoid tactile sensing.

name: PaXini Technology
description: Private Chinese maker of multidimensional tactile sensors (PX-6AX series, Hall-effect 6D force/torque) and tactile dexterous hands (DexH13) for humanoid / embodied-AI robots; full-stack tactile + hand + robot supplier candidate.

name: Bosch Sensortec
description: MEMS sensor subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH (private); high-performance IMUs (BMI088, BMI323, BMI563) explicitly targeted at robotics incl. agile humanoid and social robots. Supplier candidate for humanoid IMU/attitude sensing.

name: Hesai Group
description: Chinese LiDAR maker, dual-listed Nasdaq (HSAI) / HKEX (2525); JT-series mini 360° 3D robotics LiDAR for mobile/humanoid robots; named only LiDAR firm on Morgan Stanley's Humanoid Tech 25. Supplier candidate for humanoid depth/LiDAR perception.

name: RoboSense Technology
description: Chinese LiDAR / robotic-vision maker, HKEX-listed (2498.HK); Active Camera (AC1/AC2) fused LiDAR+RGB+IMU vision and dexterous hands for humanoid robots; partnerships with multiple humanoid firms. Supplier candidate for humanoid perception.

name: Orbbec
description: Chinese 3D-vision camera maker, Shanghai STAR-listed (688322.SS); Gemini-series stereo-vision depth cameras for robotics/embodied AI (HONOR humanoid, Reachy 2; Jetson Thor integration); reported >70% 3D-vision share in China service robots / Korea mobile robots. Supplier candidate.

name: RealSense Inc.
description: Stereo depth-camera maker spun out of Intel into a standalone private company (2025; ~$50M Series A, NVIDIA collaboration). D4xx depth cameras (e.g. D455 in Agility Digit's neck); reports working with ~60% of AMR and humanoid developers. Supplier candidate for humanoid depth/RGB perception.

name: EVE Energy
description: Public Shenzhen-listed (ChiNext) lithium-ion and all-solid-state battery cell maker; ticker 300014.SZ is mainland China A-share exposure, not a US primary listing. Cell-merchant supplier candidate; humanoid packs remain integrator-captive.

name: Molicel (E-One Moli Energy)
description: Ultra-high-power cylindrical lithium-ion cell maker; merchant cell supplier candidate listing 'humanoid robotics applications' on its product site. Not directly listed; ticker 1101.TW is its parent Taiwan Cement Corporation (TCC) Group on the Taiwan Stock Exchange, i.e. indirect parent-level exposure, not a US primary listing. Humanoid packs remain integrator-captive; Molicel supplies cells.

name: Panasonic (Panasonic Energy / Panasonic Holdings)
description: Major high-power/high-energy cylindrical lithium-ion cell maker (2170 format). Merchant cell supplier candidate; ticker 6752.T is the parent Panasonic Holdings on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (Panasonic Energy is its battery segment), i.e. Japan-listed exposure, not a US primary listing. Humanoids repurpose this high-power cylindrical cell class; packs remain integrator-captive.

name: Infineon Technologies
description: Public power-semiconductor and microcontroller maker (power switches/MOSFETs, gate drivers, battery-monitoring & balancing ICs, MCUs). Merchant-silicon supplier for humanoid power electronics / BMS front-ends; ticker IFX.DE is Frankfurt/Xetra exposure (US OTC: IFNNY), not a US primary listing. Supplies the merchant ICs; the BMS control firmware/algorithm is the robot maker's (captive).

name: NXP Semiconductors
description: Public NASDAQ-listed (NXPI) semiconductor maker; supplies battery-management ICs and standalone BMS reference designs aimed at mobile robotics (drones/rovers), plus MCUs for BMS/inverter use. Merchant-silicon supplier candidate; the pack BMS firmware/integration remains the robot maker's.

name: Qualcomm
description: Public US-listed (Nasdaq) robotics SoC supplier; markets the Dragonwing IQ10 series premium-tier onboard 'brain of the robot' processor for full-size humanoids and AMRs, and is collaborating with Figure on humanoid compute architecture. Merchant alternative to NVIDIA Jetson Thor for onboard AI compute.

name: Fuzhou Rockchip Electronics
description: Public China-listed (Shanghai) application-processor SoC designer; its RK3588/RK3588S edge SoC (octa-core, ~6 TOPS NPU) is the adopted main compute/'brain' platform in multiple Chinese humanoid robots (e.g. AgiBot/ZhiYuan Lingxi X2, LimX Oli). Low-cost merchant onboard-compute alternative to NVIDIA Jetson Thor for domestic humanoids.

name: D-Robotics
description: Privately held robot-chip spinoff of Horizon Robotics (HKEX: 9660; D-Robotics shares a technological lineage and coordinated roadmaps with it but is a separate, Series-A-funded company). Makes the RDK S100 — the industry's first single-SoC platform integrating robot 'brain' (compute) and 'cerebellum' (control), 80-128 TOPS — for developers of humanoid robots. Merchant onboard compute-control SoC.

name: Efficient Power Conversion (EPC)
description: Privately held (El Segundo, CA) gallium-nitride (GaN) power-semiconductor maker; offers the EPC91122 3-phase BLDC motor-drive inverter evaluation board engineered specifically for humanoid robot joint applications, plus GaN parts for compact wrist/finger/toe motors. Merchant GaN motor-drive/gate-driver-inverter supplier for humanoid actuators.

name: Microchip Technology
description: Public US-listed (Nasdaq) microcontroller and analog supplier; its dsPIC33 DSC-based integrated motor drivers combine a digital signal controller, a three-phase MOSFET gate driver, and LIN/CAN FD into one device for FOC BLDC/PMSM motor control. Merchant motor-drive MCU + gate-driver supplier applicable to humanoid joint/actuator drive (robotics/industrial motor-control class, humanoid design win not yet confirmed).

name: Victrex
description: Public London-listed PEEK polymer maker (VICTREX PEEK / PAEK, HPG gears); one of ~4 thousand-ton-scale PEEK producers worldwide. Markets PEEK for robotics gears, bushings/bearings, and lightweight components replacing metal. PEEK is the headline lightweighting polymer in humanoid skeletons/limbs.

name: Evonik
description: Public Frankfurt-listed specialty-chemicals maker; VESTAKEEP PEEK line (incl. tribological Easy Slide 2 slide bearings) explicitly marketed to the robotics industry. One of ~4 thousand-ton-scale PEEK producers worldwide.
